bear.writtenAnchor: Incretin demand normalises faster than the current ramp implies: competing entrants and payer pressure cap price, the FY2025 revenue step from 45,043m to 65,179m (H:revenue) proves to be a one-off peak year, and growth settles near the low single digits seen in FY2017-FY2019 (H:revenue). The very large capacity and acquisition build already embedded in invested capital — 18,556m in FY2020 to 61,770m in FY2025 (H:returns) — keeps absorbing cash, so margins sit near the weakest cash conversion the company has recently filed (operating cash flow 8,818m on 45,043m of revenue in FY2024, H:cashflow, H:revenue) and each new dollar invested earns about the discount rate or less. Stock compensation of 626m a year (H:cashflow) keeps diluting holders.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The FY2016-FY2020 stretch of the filed history grew revenue from 21.2bn to 24.5bn, about 3.7% a year, including a -5.9% year; a return to that pace is the conservative case and sits inside the filed single-year range of -5.9% to 44.7%.

operatingMargin.text: H:margin files no operating margin for any year, so the anchor is cash conversion: FY2024 operating cash flow of 8,818m on revenue of 45,043m is 19.6% and FY2022 was 26.6% (H:cashflow, H:revenue); 22% is near the weak end of that proxy band.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Capex is not disclosed, so the anchor is D&A of 2.0bn in FY2025 (about 3% of revenue) plus the recent invested-capital build; with growth slowing, net investment is cut back to roughly five points of revenue, modestly above replacement-level depreciation.

returnOnNewInvestment.text: ROIC is not filed for any year (H:returns), so the proxy is the change in operating cash flow against the change in invested capital, 10,313m on 43,214m from FY2020 to FY2025 (H:cashflow, H:returns), roughly 24%; the bear cuts that to about the discount rate on the view that recent acquisition-heavy capital additions earn far less than the historic base.

shareCount.text: Stock-based compensation has risen from 255m in FY2016 to 626m in FY2025 (H:cashflow); with no buyback disclosure supplied, the bear assumes that dilution is not offset and the count creeps up about 3% over the forecast. (1.03× today's diluted count)

base.writtenAnchor: The current product cycle keeps compounding but decelerates from its present pace: the quarter ended 2026-06-30 grew 47.7% year on year to 22,974m with trailing twelve-month revenue of 79,665m (H:quarter), well above the 13.3% nine-year window CAGR (H:revenue), so a mid-teens constant five-year rate sits between the two. Cash conversion holds near the FY2025 level — operating cash flow 16,813m on 65,179m of revenue (H:cashflow, H:revenue) — because manufacturing capacity added over FY2023-FY2025 absorbs volume without proportional spend. Reinvestment stays heavy but below the FY2025 extreme, and each incremental dollar earns well above the 10.0% terminal return implied by a narrow moat.

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The nine-year window CAGR is 13.3% and the latest quarter grew 47.7% to 22,974m with trailing twelve-month revenue of 79,665m (H:revenue, H:quarter); a 15% constant five-year rate sits just above the long-run average and well below the current pace, inside the filed single-year range.

operatingMargin.text: No operating margin is filed (H:margin), so the base uses FY2025 cash conversion, operating cash flow 16,813m on revenue 65,179m, about 25.8%, as the reference point and holds a 27% operating margin, in line with the FY2022 ratio of 26.6% (H:cashflow, H:revenue).

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: Capex is not disclosed; D&A rose from 1.5bn to 2.0bn over the decade (about 3% of revenue) while invested capital grew 17.3bn in FY2025 alone on 65.2bn of revenue, so continued capacity build at roughly eight points of revenue of net investment is the middle read.

returnOnNewInvestment.text: No ROIC is filed, so the inference is from the capital build: invested capital rose 17.3bn in FY2025 while revenue rose 20.1bn, and at the base 28% operating margin and 21% tax that incremental revenue carries roughly 4.5bn of NOPAT, about a 0.26 incremental return; 0.16 is a deliberately conservative read of that and sits above the 10.0% base terminal return (9.0% rate plus narrow moat credit).

shareCount.text: Stock-based compensation of 626m in FY2025 is about 1% of revenue and roughly 4% of operating cash flow of 16,813m (H:cashflow, H:revenue); with no buyback disclosure supplied, the base assumes only partial offset and a 1% rise in the count. (1.01× today's diluted count)

bull.writtenAnchor: Capacity built out through FY2025 (invested capital 61,770m, H:returns) is filled at high utilisation while demand continues at something like the latest quarter's 47.7% year-on-year pace (H:quarter), so revenue compounds at the upper end of the filed single-year range (H:revenue) for five years before fading. Operating leverage lifts cash conversion above the FY2025 ratio of 16,813m on 65,179m (H:cashflow, H:revenue), the reinvestment needed per dollar of revenue falls as the heaviest build years pass, and incremental returns stay close to the roughly 24% after-tax cash return on the capital added between FY2020 and FY2025 (H:cashflow, H:returns). Share count is held flat as cash flow covers stock compensation of 626m (H:cashflow).

revenueGrowthOrPath.text: The latest quarter grew 47.7% year on year to 22,974m and trailing twelve-month revenue is 79,665m against FY2025's 65,179m (H:quarter, H:revenue); 22% for five years is roughly half the current pace and sits inside the filed single-year range, which reached 44.7%.

operatingMargin.text: H:margin files no margin, so the ceiling is set from cash conversion, which improved from 19.6% of revenue in FY2024 to 25.8% in FY2025 as volume filled new capacity (H:cashflow, H:revenue); the bull extends that trend a few points further to 32%.

reinvestmentCapitalIntensity.text: With the FY2023-FY2025 build already in invested capital (33,070m to 61,770m, H:returns) and D&A only 1,997m (H:capex), the bull assumes net investment falls to 10% of revenue as the installed capacity is filled rather than extended (H:revenue).

returnOnNewInvestment.text: FY2025 added 20.1bn of revenue against a 17.3bn rise in invested capital; at the bull 33% margin and 21% tax that is roughly 5.2bn of incremental NOPAT, about a 0.30 implied incremental return, so 0.22 is a restrained figure and clears the 11.5% bull terminal return (9.0% rate, narrow moat credit, bull add-on).

shareCount.text: Stock compensation of 626m is small against FY2025 operating cash flow of 16,813m (H:cashflow), so the bull assumes dilution is fully offset and the diluted count is unchanged; no buyback disclosure was supplied, so no reduction is taken. (1× today's diluted count)

moatAnchor.text: Intangible assets — patent-protected branded medicines, supported by regulatory approval barriers. Revenue rose from 21,222m in FY2016 to 65,179m in FY2025 while invested capital rose from 18,274m to 61,770m, and operating cash flow rose from 4,851m to 16,813m, implying roughly a 24% after-tax return on the capital added over FY2020-FY2025 (10,313m of added cash flow on 43,214m of added capital). Because H:returns files no ROIC for any year, that incremental cash return is the only filed evidence of pricing power, so the credit is held to narrow (+1.0 point, terminal return 10.0%) rather than wide, and the terminal return stays below the realised incremental return.

constantsAnchor.text: No company tax disclosure was supplied, so the NOPAT tax rate uses the general US federal statutory rate of 21.0% (STATUTORY), the same rate already applied in H:returns. H:margin files no current or median operating margin, so the stress margin is set from the weakest recent cash conversion — operating cash flow of 8,818m on revenue of 45,043m in FY2024, about 19.6% (H:cashflow, H:revenue) — and held at 20%, below the bear operating margin.
